chunks: And Ayatullah al-Allama al-Hilli said in al-Khulasa:

'... Among the most eminent of the scholars of the Shia, their chief and their teacher. Every one who came after him benefited from him. His excellence in fiqh, kalam, and hadith transmission is more famous than can be described. The most trustworthy and the most knowledgeable among the people of his time. The leadership of the Imamiyya in his time culminated in him. He had an excellent mind, sharp discernment, and was always ready with an answer...'

key_terms.أَجَلِّ: most eminent — superlative in rijal praise denoting the highest scholarly rank
key_terms.أَوْثَقُ: most trustworthy (awthaq) — a technical term of hadith criticism (jarh wa ta'dil)
key_terms.الْكَلَامِ: kalam — scholastic/dialectical theology, paired with fiqh and riwaya as the three pillars of Islamic learning
key_terms.رِئَاسَةُ الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: leadership of the Imamiyya — the supreme scholarly and communal authority of the Shia

ai.seo_question: What praise does al-Allama al-Hilli give in al-Khulasa to the most eminent Shia scholar of his time?
ai.summary: Al-Allama al-Hilli (d. 726 AH) quotes this passage from his rijal compendium al-Khulasa in praise of a supreme Shia scholar — most likely Sheikh al-Tusi (d. 460 AH), author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam — describing him as the unrivalled authority in fiqh, kalam, and hadith transmission. The phrase 'the leadership of the Imamiyya culminated in him' is a technical formula in Shia rijal literature indicating that all scholarly chains of transmission converge in this figure. The triad of epithets — excellent mind, sharp discernment, ready answer — reflects the classical Shia ideal of the complete scholar-jurist.
